# Spec-Kit Studio: Full Project Brief

## Identity

Spec-Kit Studio is an open-source, local-first developer workspace for reviewable specification-driven development. Its canonical project page is https://rraviku2-uhg.github.io/spec-kit-studio/ and its canonical source repository is https://github.com/rraviku2_uhg/spec-kit-studio. It is licensed under Apache-2.0.

Spec-Kit Studio is built around GitHub Spec Kit concepts but is an independent project. Do not describe it as an official GitHub product.

## Problem and purpose

Coding agents can generate files quickly, but teams still need durable answers to five questions: what was requested, what scope was approved, what changed, what evidence was produced, and what still requires a human decision. Spec-Kit Studio keeps those answers connected from intake through handoff.

The product is intended for software teams using AI coding agents, specification-driven development, structured planning, isolated Git worktrees, and evidence-based review. It does not replace product judgment, code review, CI, accessibility testing, security review, or release controls.

## Core workflow

1. Connect a local repository and record Git, stack, tool, and baseline evidence.
2. Select a feature or one independently deliverable user story.
3. Review the specification, impact map, persona evidence, architecture decisions, and ordered tasks.
4. Audit artifacts before implementation.
5. Run an approved task in an isolated linked worktree with an explicitly selected local coding agent.
6. Retain changed files, command output, checks, and recovery context as a review receipt.
7. Verify the outcome and export a repository-relative handoff package. The completed developer handoff distinguishes strict engine artifacts, Studio review evidence, and application code.
8. After the developer has committed and pushed the clean linked-worktree branch, optionally create a GitHub PR through the local GitHub CLI session. Studio records the PR details in delivery evidence; it never commits, pushes, merges, or deploys.

Studio also supports independent Bug Fix and Idea Assessment workflows. Those workflows preserve their own evidence and do not silently advance the main Feature Journey.

## Trust and privacy boundaries

The browser workspace stores project state locally. An optional loopback connector performs local repository operations. The connector listens on localhost, confines paths to configured roots, supports a pairing token, and requires explicit confirmation for writes, worktree creation, checks, tool installation, and agent execution.

Cloud AI is optional and disabled until an operator configures it. Generated text, audit scores, passing checks, and agent output remain review candidates rather than automatic approval.

GovCloud and DoD are fail-closed deployment modes, not certification claims. They require enterprise identity and disable external AI egress unless an approved in-boundary adapter is configured. When active, Studio displays a persistent deployment-boundary banner on every screen.

## Supported environment and integrations

- Runtime: Node.js 22.12 or later within Node 22.
- Operating systems: Windows, macOS, and Linux.
- Prompt targets: Codex, Claude, GitHub Copilot CLI, Gemini, and Cursor.
- Optional integrations: GitHub repositories, GitHub App authentication, enterprise SSO/OIDC, Jira, and Gemini-backed generation.
- Main implementation: React, TypeScript, Vite, Express, Tailwind CSS, and IndexedDB-backed browser state.
- SDD engines: GitHub Spec Kit v1.0.6 is the only verified strict adapter. OpenSpec, BMAD Method, Tessl, AWS Kiro, and Custom remain future-facing profiles until a verified adapter is shipped.
- Personas: Product Manager, Business Analyst, Developer/Architect, and Security Researcher prepare accepted, feature-scoped artifacts. Those artifacts are read-only inputs only where Studio's declared consumption policy permits them.

## Terminology

- Feature Journey: the eight-stage review path from connection through handoff.
- Connected Workspace: repository connection, scanning, tool detection, and baseline evidence.
- Delivery item: one feature or one independently deliverable user story with its own artifacts and receipts.
- Linked worktree: the isolated Git worktree used for implementation.
- Receipt: retained evidence from a bounded implementation or verification action.
- Outcome Refinery: a bounded repair loop for comparing expected and delivered outcomes while retaining evidence.
